formula_applied: FAA profile formula (profiles/faa/config/tco-analyzer.yaml -> profiles/faa/skills/tco-analyzer/references/faa-tco-definition.md): Application cost = Cloud/Infra hosting + O&M + hosting, per the FAA Announcement Element 7 footnote. Operational costs only; one-time development/modernization costs and user-organization-side costs (workstation hardware, training) are excluded by definition.
assumptions: No CMDB export, billing/invoice extract, hosting bill, support contract, or license agreement was provided or found for this application at onboarding (catalog.json open_questions and structural-analysis.json both record this gap independently) — there is no cost ledger to collect line items from, so this baseline is derived entirely from the confirmed architecture rather than from financial records.

Cloud/Infra hosting is set to $0: structural-analysis.json confirms the application's only deployment surface is 'Student Management System.exe', a single Windows desktop executable manually installed per workstation against a local .accdb file opened via a hardcoded file path — there is no server, VM, container, or cloud resource for FAA to host. Per-workstation compute is excluded from the FAA TCO definition as a user-organization-side cost.

Shared hosting is set to $0: the structural analysis found zero use of shared middleware, shared databases, identity providers, or API gateways — the application has no network surface and no integration points, so there is no shared-infrastructure cost to apportion to it.

O&M is set to $0: no business owner, operational criticality rating, support staff, or SRE/DevOps allocation for this application could be identified in any Discovery artifact; it is documented as a single-developer, GPL-licensed academic/portfolio project with a one-commit git history and no CI/CD. Absent any evidence of ongoing FAA-funded operations or maintenance labor, no O&M figure is asserted.

No licensing cost is attributed: the database is Microsoft Access (Jet/ACE OLEDB) accessed via a bundled .accdb file, and the application itself is GPL-licensed with a public GitHub origin: no FAA-paid license was identified.

GOVERNING-PROFILE / SCOPE DISCREPANCY (carried forward, not newly adjudicated here): this task's governing profile is declared as 'faa', and this baseline applies the FAA profile's TCO formula as instructed. However, both catalog.json and structural-analysis.json independently flag that the application's source, README, and project report describe a generic student-record-management desktop tool with no detectable aviation, NAS, air-traffic, or FAA business relevance. This baseline does not adopt or assert any alternative governing profile; it applies the FAA formula as directed and flags the same scope mismatch for the engagement owner to resolve before this baseline is used in portfolio governance (P6.2) or cost-savings certification (P6.3) decisions.

Confidence is rated 'low' because every figure above is a reasoned absence of cost (no server/shared-infra/support-contract exists to price) rather than a measured figure drawn from a bill, invoice, or CMDB record; if a CMDB/billing extract or an authoritative business-owner statement surfaces later, this baseline should be revisited.
